document.abstract: The increasing use of digital equipment in television studios brings with it potential problems for the maintenance engineer when diagnosing faults. The paper considers the reasons for this, the levels at which diagnosis is required and some of the techniques that can be used.

authors.bio: David J. Bradshaw has been with the engineering division of the British Broadcasting Corp. since 1965, initially as a design engineer in the designs department and subsequently as head of video section. He is a member of the European Broadcasting Unions group, which produced recommendations for fault diagnosis procedures in digital production equipment.
